votes.evidence: Mechanics confirmed: products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:809 process_pull_request_event is a Celery @shared_task; :876 calls _inbox_rereview_carve_out only when _review_skip_reason is set; the carve-out (:167-185) gates on action in {"synchronize","reopened"} or base retarget, bot author (:124), head repo == base repo (:175-177), and an enabled StamphogRepoConfig with installation_id and connected_by_user_id, then calls find_signal_implementation_run (:191-196). products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:500-506 delegates to webhooks.find_task_run; the pr_url leg is indexed (models.py:1153-1157 task_run_output_pr_url_idx) and on a miss webhooks.py:64-77 runs TaskRun.objects.filter(branch=..., task__repository__iexact=..., state__wizard_head_branch__isnull=True). TaskRun.branch (models.py:1081) and Task.repository (models.py:175-177) have no index in Meta.indexes (:1147-1174 and :244-250) and no migration under products/tasks/backend/migrations adds one; webhooks.py has no cache use. So a bot-PR synchronize on an enabled repo does run one unindexed query.
votes.refutation: Not a defect. The identical unindexed branch leg already runs on every `opened` PR on every repo with the GitHub App installed (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:129-159: `opened` and `closed` both reach find_task_run, and a brand-new PR URL never matches the pr_url leg), so this cost profile is the accepted baseline for all PR traffic. The PR adds only synchronize/reopened/retarget events for bot-authored, repo-native PRs on the few enabled StamphogRepoConfig repos, executed in a Celery worker, not a request path: one two-table equality scan a few times per hour, no N+1, no per-tenant growth, no user-visible latency. The suggested fix (skip the branch fallback when pr_url misses) would defeat the facade's stated purpose (api.py docstring: match like the backstop because a self-driving run may not yet have recorded its PR URL) and regress identification; an index for a query this infrequent is not warranted. Real but sub-threshold, and duplicating an already-accepted pattern.

votes.evidence:
Premise partially holds: neither column is indexed. /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/tasks/backend/models.py:175-177 declares `Task.repository` as a plain CharField, and the Task Meta indexes at :244-250 list nothing for it; `TaskRun.branch` (:1081) has no entry in the TaskRun Meta indexes at :1147-1174 (only pr_url, wizard_head_branch, created_at, task, team/stage/task). No migration adds a raw index either (grep of products/tasks/backend/migrations/ for branch/repository + index/CREATE returns only the 0001 column definition). The branch leg at products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:64-72 filters `branch=..., task__repository__iexact=...` on that unindexed pair.

But the finding's claim that this PR ships a scale-biting defect fails on three counts:

1. The unindexed branch leg is already on a higher-volume, ungated path. products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:141-159 (`handle_pull_request_event`) calls `find_task_run(pr_url=..., branch=..., repository=...)` on EVERY `opened` and `closed` pull_request webhook for every repo the GitHub App is installed on, with no bot-author, head-repo, or StamphogRepoConfig gate. On `opened`, the pr_url leg (:37-58) always misses for a brand-new PR URL, so the branch leg already runs once per opened PR fleet-wide. The carve-out adds only the `synchronize`/`reopened`/base-retarget subset (`_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS` = {"synchronize","reopened"}, products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:49, checked at :167).

2. The carve-out is triple-gated before the query runs, so "every bot PR event" is contradicted by the code: tasks.py:170-173 returns early for non-bot authors; :176-178 returns early unless `head.repo.full_name` equals the event repo (repo-native only); :179-186 returns early unless a synced, enabled StamphogRepoConfig with installation_id and connected_by_user_id exists. It is reached only when `_review_skip_reason` is non-None (:872-876). It runs in a Celery task (`process_pull_request_event`), not a request path.

3. The suggested cheap fix ("skip the branch fallback when pr_url was supplied and matched nothing") is contradicted by an existing test and by the backstop's documented purpose. products/tasks/backend/tests/test_webhooks.py:1273-1283 `test_branch_match_covers_runs_without_a_recorded_pr_url` asserts `find_signal_implementation_run(pr_url=<unrecorded>, head_branch=...)` must still resolve the run by branch. webhooks.py:169-173 explains why: the backstop exists precisely for runs whose output carries no PR URL yet. Dropping the branch leg would break positive identification of the self-driving PRs the carve-out exists for.

Corroboration that the pattern was accepted rather than a shipped defect: local `master` (b375d31315c, which already contains this merged code plus later changes) still runs the same generic `branch=branch` leg with no index (`git show master:products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py` lines ~118-127). The later `task_run_sd_branch_idx` added on master (models.py:2302-2309 on master) indexes a different key, `state__self_driving_head_branch`, added for a misattribution-correctness reason, and leaves the generic branch leg unindexed. The existing dependabot-shaped test, products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:874-888 `test_inbox_carve_out_requires_task_linkage`, covers the behavioral contract (no review, no run) and mocks `find_signal_implementation_run`, so no test asserts on query cost, consistent with it being treated as sub-threshold.
votes.refutation: The "unindexed" part is true, but the finding frames a pre-existing, accepted query pattern as a new scale defect introduced by this PR. The identical unindexed branch fallback already executes on every `opened` PR webhook across every installed repo with no gating at all (webhooks.py:141-159), which dwarfs the carve-out's increment: synchronize/reopened events on bot-authored, repo-native-head PRs on the small set of repos with a synced+enabled StamphogRepoConfig, executed in a Celery worker. No concrete user-visible or infrastructure impact is reachable from that increment. The finding's proposed cheapest fix would break `test_branch_match_covers_runs_without_a_recorded_pr_url` and defeat the backstop's stated purpose. Adding an index would be a legitimate standalone efficiency improvement to the pre-existing fallback, but that is a separate, general tasks-webhook optimization, not a defect this PR ships. Not real as a PR finding; severity null.

votes.evidence:
Reachability (angle 3): the trigger IS reachable in production. In /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py, the celery task calls `_review_skip_reason(pr)` (line ~870), which returns "bot" for dependabot/renovate, and then always runs `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` on the skip path (line 876). The carve-out's gates (lines 167-183) are: action in `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS = {"synchronize", "reopened"}` (line 49) or base retarget; `_is_bot_authored` (lines 124-127: user.type == "Bot" or "[bot]" in login); head.repo.full_name == repo (dependabot/renovate push repo-native branches, so this passes); and a StamphogRepoConfig that is enabled + has installation_id + connected_by_user_id (lines 289-304). A dependabot rebase on any stamphog-enabled repo satisfies all four, so `find_signal_implementation_run` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:484-516) runs, its pr_url leg (served by `task_run_output_pr_url_idx`, models.py:1153-1157) misses, and the branch leg in products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:64-77 executes `TaskRun.objects.filter(branch=..., task__repository__iexact=..., state__wizard_head_branch__isnull=True).first()`. Neither `Task.repository` (models.py:175-177, Meta indexes 245-251 list none for it) nor `TaskRun.branch` (models.py:1081, indexes 1147-1174) is indexed. So the factual premise holds.

What makes it not a defect: the identical unindexed branch fallback already runs on master's tasks backstop for every `opened` PR on every repo delivering to the unified GitHub webhook (webhooks.py:141-159), where the pr_url leg can never match a just-opened PR — including every dependabot/renovate `opened` PR everywhere. That path was accepted without an index. This PR only adds `synchronize`/`reopened` deliveries for bot-authored, repo-native PRs on the handful of stamphog-configured repos, i.e. a strictly narrower event class than the pre-existing one. The query is one two-table equality join over internal-scale tables (PostHog Code tasks/runs), executed in a Celery worker that already does a per-event DB read (`_resolve_repo_config` on the same skip path, tasks.py:895), with no N+1 and no unbounded growth. The finding itself is already marked `is_valid: false` in GB.json with a validator note reaching the same conclusion.
votes.refutation: I tried to refute the claim by finding a guard that keeps dependabot synchronize events off the branch leg: there is none — the bot check, fork check, and config check all pass for a dependabot rebase on a stamphog-enabled repo, and the pr_url leg misses because no TaskRun records a dependabot PR URL. I also looked for an index in the PR's migrations serving (branch, lower(repository)); there is none (only `task_run_output_pr_url_idx` and `task_run_wizard_branch_idx`). So the mechanical claim survives. The refutation that does hold is on defect status rather than reachability: the same unindexed query already runs on master on a larger event class (every `opened` PR on every repo), so this PR neither introduces the unindexed path nor materially changes its cost profile; a handful of extra millisecond-scale queries per hour in a background worker is not a performance problem that bites at real scale. `should_fix` is unwarranted; at most this is an index-hygiene note that belongs to the pre-existing backstop, not this PR.
